BILL NUMBER:  S4589

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the public health law, in relation to providing for
the establishment of a uniform letter grading system to classify
inspection results for food places

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
Directs the commissioner of health to establish and implement a
uniform letter grading system to classify inspection results for food
places and requires that inspection grades be posted in a conspicuous
location near the entrance of each food service establishment.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
Adds a new subdivision 3 to section 1350 of the public health law
which directs the commissioner of health to establish and implement a
uniform letter grading system to classify inspection results for food
places.  Requires any establishment engaged in the preparation, sale
or service of food for and to the general public to display the letter
grade received on its most recent inspection in a conspicuous
location.

 JUSTIFICATION :
The New York State Department of Health is charged with inspecting and
supervising all public places in New York in which food is prepared,
sold or served, including restaurants and cafeterias. Inspectors from
local health departments conduct unannounced inspections of food
service establishments to evaluate the safety and sanitation of the
premises, and monitor food handling practices to ensure adequate
compliance with state and local laws. An unfortunate effect of
county-level enforcement is that the evaluation criteria and grading
systems can vary widely between jurisdictions, making it difficult for
consumers reading an inspection report to know whether an
establishment has passed or failed.  A clear, concise system of letter
grades would make it easier for consumers to make an informed dining
decision and allow more meaningful comparisons across jurisdictions.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
2004:  A.2702 - Referred to the Health Committee
2006:  S.2696 - Referred to Health
2008:  S.2243 - Referred to Health

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the one hundred twentieth day after it
shall have become a law; provided that the commissioner of health is
authorized to promulgate any and all rules and regulations and take
any other measures necessary to implement this act on its effective
date on or before such date.

B.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to the establishment of a letter grading system to classify inspection results for certain public food service establishments
B.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4589B

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the public health law, in relation to the
establishment of a letter grading system to classify inspection
results for certain public food service establishments


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
The Commissioner of Health shall establish and implement a uniform
grading system consisting of letters A, B, C, D and F, to classify
inspection results for public food service establishments. Such
inspection grades shall be posted in a conspicuous location near the
entrance of each food service establishment. Such letter grades (A
through F) and the criteria for designating such letter grades shall
be established by Rule and shall be set by the Department of Health
(DOH) based on objective criteria that evaluates each public food
service establishment's sanitation and food handling practices.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
Section 1: Adds a new Public Health Law Section 1352-d that directs
DOH to establish and implement a uniform letter grading system to
classify inspection results for places that serve food to the general
public. Requires establishments engaged in the preparation, sale or
service of food for the general public to display the letter grade
received on its most recent inspection in a conspicuous location.
Under the general provisions of the Public Health Law and the State
Sanitary Code, such program and the criteria for establishing such a
program should be implemented pursuant to rules promulgated by DOH.
Pursuant to the State Administrative Procedure Act and the State
Sanitary Code, each public food service establishment may appeal, on
an expedited basis, the letter grade assigned to it and petition for a
different letter grade. DOH, in establishing criteria for awarding a
restaurant's letter grade, shall consider only the conditions of a
food service establishment related to its food handling practices and
the general sanitary condition of such premises.

 JUSTIFICATION :
DOH is charged with inspecting and supervising all public places in
New York in which food is prepared, sold or served, including
restaurants and cafeterias. Inspectors from local health departments
conduct unannounced inspections of food service establishments to
evaluate the safety and sanitation of the premises, and monitor food
handling practices to ensure adequate compliance with state and local
laws. An unfortunate effect of county-level enforcement is that the
evaluation criteria and grading systems can vary widely between
jurisdictions, making it difficult for consumers reading an inspection
report to know whether an establishment's sanitary conditions are of
the highest quality or some lower level with regard to sanitation and
general cleanliness. A clear, concise system of letter grades would
make it easier for consumers to make an informed dining decision and
allow for more meaningful comparisons across jurisdictions. Further,
such grading system will encourage all restaurants to more vigilantly
upgrade their cleanliness and sanitation standards.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
2004: A.2702 - Referred to the Health Committee
2006: S.2696 - Referred to Health
2008: S.2243 - Referred to Health

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect one year after it shall have become a law.
The commissioner of health is authorized to promulgate any and all
rules and regulations and take any other measures necessary to
implement this act on its effective date on or before such date.
